messages.content: Help me execute the test runner `runThis` with arguments to set the wait time to 2 minutes and output the logs to a specific print stream `testLogStream`, considering the debuggee name is 'TestDebuggee'?

function.name: runThis
function.description: Executes the test runner with provided arguments and a print stream for logging. It handles the debuggee binding, output redirection, and test execution flow. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

argv.description: An array of strings representing the command-line arguments, to include waittime and debuggeeName. Format: -waitTime, <waitTime>, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee This is Java Array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation.

out.description: The PrintStream to output the logs to. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function runThis with argv string and out string. The argv should be an array of strings: "-waitTime", "120000", "-debuggeeName", "TestDebuggee". Wait time in milliseconds? They said 2 minutes. So 120000 ms. Provide as string representation of Java array type. In the description: "An array of strings representing the command-line arguments, to include waittime and debuggeeName. Format: -waitTime, <waitTime>, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee This is Java Array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation." So we need to provide something like "[\"-waitTime\", \"120000\", \"-debuggeeName\", \"TestDebuggee\"]" but maybe just a string representation of array: "[-waitTime, 120000, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee]"? But they say elements are of type String; they are not in string representation. That means we don't wrap them in quotes? Actually "they are not in string representation" might mean we don't double quote them. So we could pass "[-waitTime, 120000, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee]". But I'm not sure.

Also out: "The PrintStream to output the logs to. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation." So we need to pass "testLogStream"? Or maybe "PrintStream(testLogStream)"? Probably just "testLogStream".

Thus call:

{
  "argv": "[-waitTime, 120000, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee]",
  "out": "testLogStream"
}

Let's produce that.
